verdicts.reason: A has a sensible top-down stack with clear headline and CTA, but the badges are centred above a left-aligned headline (and stacked in reverse order), and 'Saturday' nearly touches the right edge. B jams the body copy against the headline with no gap, makes the logo oversized, leaves a dead gap mid-canvas, and strands the FREE badge alone at the bottom, away from LIMITED SPOTS.

A is the same broken layout: body copy collides with the headline, the logo is oversized, and the FREE badge is orphaned under the CTA. B keeps the badges grouped and spacing even, but it mixes a left-aligned text block with centred badges, logo and CTA. The logo also sits between the copy and the CTA, which breaks the reading flow.

A again has a cramped headline and body, an oversized logo, and the FREE badge stranded at the bottom, separated from its partner badge. B reads in the best order (logo, headline, copy, badges, CTA) and keeps groups together. It still mixes left-aligned text with centred elements, the headline runs nearly to the right edge, and the bottom margin is tight.
